introduction: On this Sunday, Jeremiah, surrounded by enemies, trusts that the Lord is with him like a mighty warrior. In the Gospel, Jesus tells his disciples three times, Do not be afraid; the Father who cares for every sparrow knows even the hairs of our heads. Paul contrasts the sin that came through Adam with the far greater grace that came through Jesus Christ. Let us proclaim the Gospel without fear.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord hears the needy. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim from the housetops what Jesus has told her. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians who are persecuted for their faith: that they may not be afraid, and know that the Father cares for them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are falsely accused or surrounded by enemies: that the Lord may defend them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who live in fear: that they may know they are of more value than many sparrows. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may acknowledge Jesus before others with courage. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you care for every sparrow and know every hair on our heads. Free us from fear, and give us courage to bear witness to your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Do not be afraid
reflection.body:
Jeremiah's life as a prophet was full of danger. In the first reading he hears people whispering against him, even "all my familiar friends, those who watch for my fall." But in the middle of this, he finds courage: "But the LORD is with me as an awesome mighty one." And he ends by praising God, "for he has delivered the soul of the needy from the hand of evildoers."

In the Gospel, Jesus is preparing his disciples to go out on mission. He knows they will meet opposition. Three times he tells them not to be afraid.

First, the truth will come out: "there is nothing covered that will not be revealed." So they must speak openly: "What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops."

Second, there is something worse than death: "Don't be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul." Physical harm is not the worst evil; losing one's soul is.

Third, and most tenderly, God cares for us in every detail. Sparrows were sold for almost nothing, yet "Not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father's will." And "the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Therefore don't be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows."

Jesus ends with a promise and a warning: "Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven."

Paul reminds us that grace is stronger than sin: through Adam, sin and death entered the world, but "much more did the grace of God" abound through Jesus Christ.

This week, name one fear that holds you back from living your faith openly, and give it to God. Remember that you are known and loved in every detail. And speak about your faith to someone, simply and without fear.
